points.why: Says the groups are answering different questions, that a 'settling' model will be attacked through its weakest assumptions, and that blame is the wrong target.

Recommends drawing out each group's views and lists the water-balance terms, but never asks for explicit agreement on the boundary, never treats rainfall as an outside input, and never records who was consulted versus only informed.
Names the commons structure (shared, finite, unpriced stock where restraint just hands water to others) and points to collective rules like metering and allocation instead of blame.
Keeps the model as a water-balance and scenario tool built live with stakeholders, which in substance covers testing hypotheses such as drought.

pitfalls.why: Explicitly advises against delivering a blame verdict and recommends building the model with stakeholders.
